title: Affine realization and pullback of Fitting ideal sheaves and their closed strata
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal F$ a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and $r\in\mathbb N$. Let $\mathcal I=\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)$ be the ideal sheaf constructed in [def-trf-fitting-ideal-sheaf] as the largest quasi-coherent ideal satisfying its affine kernel-minor bounds. For every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$, every finite generating surjection $A^n\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F(U)$, and its kernel $K\subset A^n$, $\mathcal I|_U$ is the ideal sheaf associated to the ideal generated by all $(n-r)$-minors of matrices with rows in $K$ [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change], with unit ideal when $n\le r$. Thus this largest-ideal construction realizes the affine minor ideals themselves, and the associated closed subscheme $Z_r(\mathcal F)\hookrightarrow S$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] restricts to $\operatorname{Spec}(A/\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F(U)))$ on $U$. For every morphism of schemes $h:T\to S$, the ordinary pullback $h^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is finite-type quasi-coherent, and there is an equality of ideal subsheaves of $\mathcal O_T$:
$$\operatorname{Fit}_r(h^*\mathcal F)=\operatorname{im}(h^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_T)=h^{-1}\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal O_T.$$
Consequently $Z_r(h^*\mathcal F)$ is canonically isomorphic over $T$ to $T\times_S Z_r(\mathcal F)$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with the given closed immersions. No finite presentation, Noetherianity or flatness is assumed; the ideal on $T$ is the image ideal, not an assertion that the map $h^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_T$ is injective.

proof.text: For every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, finite type of $\mathcal F$ implies that $M_U=\mathcal F(U)$ is a finitely generated $A$-module by part (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine], so a finite generating surjection $\pi:A^n\twoheadrightarrow M_U$ exists. For any such $\pi$, [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-sheaf-affine-sections] gives $\mathcal I(U)=I_r(\pi)$ and $\mathcal I|_U=\widetilde{I_r(\pi)}\subseteq\mathcal O_U$, with the unit ideal when $n\leq r$. By part (1) of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] this ideal does not depend on $\pi$; call it $I_U=\operatorname{Fit}_r(M_U)$. This is the first assertion of the statement.

source.place: Tag 0C3C (section-fitting-ideals), first construction; More on Algebra Tags 07Z8 and 07ZA

proof.text: The affine counit identifies $\mathcal F|_U$ with $\widetilde{M_U}$. The principal-open section formula for the associated module then identifies the restriction $M_U\to\mathcal F(U_f)$ with $M_U\to(M_U)_f$. By the localization clause of independence/base change, $I_{U_f}=I_U A_f$. Principal opens are affine with structure-ring restriction $A\to A_f$, as stated in the affine-ideals gluing lemma. Thus the family $(I_U)$ satisfies exactly that lemma's compatibility hypothesis; no claim that arbitrary intersections of affine opens are affine is needed.

source.place: Tag 0C3C (section-fitting-ideals), localization justification; Schemes Tags 01IA and 01HV

proof.text: Apply the affine-ideals gluing lemma [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme] to the family $(I_U)$ of step 2: it gives a closed immersion $i:Z\to S$ whose ideal sheaf $\mathcal J$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] satisfies $\mathcal J(U)=I_U$ for every affine open $U$, and $i^{-1}(U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A/I_U)$ over $U$. By step 1, $\mathcal J(U)=\mathcal I(U)$ on every affine open. Both are subsheaves of $\mathcal O_S$ and affine opens cover every open, so membership of a section is tested on an affine cover by the sheaf gluing axiom and $\mathcal J=\mathcal I$. Thus $Z_r(\mathcal F)=Z$ is the closed subscheme cut out by $\mathcal I$, and $Z_r(\mathcal F)|_U=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F(U)))$.

Put $\mathcal G=h^*\mathcal F$. Apply [lem-trf-fitting-sheaf-arbitrary-pullback] to $h$, $\mathcal F$ and $r$. It shows that $\mathcal G$ is finite-type quasi-coherent; that for affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq T$ with $h(V)\subseteq U$ and induced ring map $\varphi:A\to B$, $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal G)(V)=\varphi(\mathcal I(U))B$; and that $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal G)=h^{-1}\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal O_T$. No flatness or finite presentation is used there. Since $\mathcal G$ satisfies the hypotheses of the statement on $T$, steps 1--3 apply to $\mathcal G$ as well: $Z_r(\mathcal G)\to T$ is the closed immersion with ideal sheaf $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal G)$.

Let $q:T\times_S Z_r(\mathcal F)\to T$. By [lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image], $q$ is a closed immersion and its ideal sheaf $\mathcal K$ is $\operatorname{im}(h^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_T)$. By [lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension], for every pair of affine opens $V\subseteq h^{-1}(U)$ as in step 4, $\mathcal K(V)$ is the ideal generated by $\varphi(\mathcal I(U))$ (same $\varphi$). By step 4 this equals $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal G)(V)$. Such $V$ inside a given open $W\subseteq T$ cover $W$: around $t\in W$ take an affine $U\ni h(t)$ and an affine $V\ni t$ inside $h^{-1}(U)\cap W$. Both are subsheaves of $\mathcal O_T$, so membership is tested on such covers and $\mathcal K=\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal G)$. With the last equality of step 4 this proves $\operatorname{Fit}_r(h^*\mathcal F)=\operatorname{im}(h^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_T)=h^{-1}\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal O_T$; injectivity of $h^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_T$ is not claimed.

The two closed immersions $Z_r(\mathcal G)\to T$ and $T\times_S Z_r(\mathcal F)\to T$ have the same ideal sheaf, by steps 4 and 5. The ideal-inclusion factorization lemma applied in both directions gives maps over $T$ between them. Their composites are identities: a closed immersion is a monomorphism directly from its definition, since its underlying map is injective and its structure-sheaf map is surjective, so a map into it over $T$ has its point map and sheaf map uniquely determined. Thus the two maps are inverse and unique over $T$. This gives the claimed canonical isomorphism with its closed immersion.
